heroHeadline: Trump: Deal 'Largely Negotiated' — Axios Publishes Nuclear Terms (HEU Export, 12–15yr Moratorium, IAEA Access); Iran: '3–4 More Days'; Brent Crude Falls to ~$96/bbl; Day 86
heroSubtitle: Day 86 (May 24): President Trump declared the US-Iran deal 'largely negotiated' on Truth Social, while simultaneously telling Axios it was '50/50.' Axios published exclusive deal parameters: Iran to export ~1,000 lbs of highly enriched uranium, accept a 12–15 year enrichment moratorium (splitting the difference between Iran's 5-year and the US's initial 20-year demand), and allow IAEA snap inspections — the US quietly dropped its 'zero enrichment' permanence demand. Iranian FM spokesman Baghaei said viewpoints are 'getting closer' but cautioned it will take '3–4 more days.' Secretary Rubio upgraded his language to 'significant progress, although not final.' Iran signaled Hormuz shipping would recover to pre-war levels within 30 days of a deal signing. Oil markets responded: Brent fell to ~$96/bbl and WTI to ~$88/bbl — among the largest weekly drops since the conflict began. On May 23 (Day 85), Pakistan Army Chief Munir completed a 'short but highly productive' Tehran visit alongside Interior Minister Naqvi; Iran, US, and Pakistan all publicly acknowledged 'encouraging' progress. IDF struck a Hezbollah underground weapons site in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley and infrastructure near Tyre on May 23, wounding a Lebanese army soldier — the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire extension continues to fray.
